gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold issue is the missing boundedness hypothesis needed for a finite enclosing radius and the resulting reconstruction construction. ISSUE-003 instead diagnoses use of the reconstruction identity at numerical tuples outside its already stated admissible time range; it does not identify that the introductory Lipschitz-domain class may contain unbounded domains or require restriction to bounded domains.

The gold defect is the undefined p=0 endpoint in the definition and maximization of C_p, together with the missing value C_0=1. ISSUE-002 concerns an anisotropic Gaussian product, its mass, and a wrong normalization factor in a reconstruction identity; it contains no recognition of the p=0 endpoint or the piecewise definition of C_p.

The gold issue is that the theorem leaves alpha free even though its estimate requires the balanced choice alpha=delta^(2/s), with a resulting counterexample for fixed nonzero alpha. ISSUE-001 addresses support and Cauchy-data conditions for cutoff-supported waves and does not diagnose the unbound regularization parameter or its required scaling.

The gold issue is the invalid replacement of a finite-tau boundary-wave integral by an exact Radon value: only a tau-to-infinity limit and a finite-tau approximation error are justified. ISSUE-001 instead concerns whether cutoff-supported waves satisfy endpoint Cauchy data so that uniqueness can identify them with solutions; it does not recognize the finite-tau-versus-limit distinction or the associated approximation error.
